## Classes

### <a name="greenbone"></a>`greenbone`

Manages the apt repository, packages, system user/group, runtime directories,
and the GMP transport credentials file used by gvm_* resource providers.

Declare this class before any gvm_* resource types. The database, redis,
service, feed, and admin sub-classes must be included separately (or via
the greenbone::server convenience class) so each concern can be ordered
correctly relative to other catalog resources.

##### <a name="-greenbone--install_method"></a>`install_method`

Data type: `Enum['unmanaged', 'docker']`

How Greenbone is installed on the node.
'unmanaged' (default): Greenbone runs natively on the host. Puppet manages
the system user/group and runtime directories, plus the apt repository
(`manage_repo`) and the packages (`manage_packages`). For a source build or
out-of-band packaging, set both of those to false. The apt install path is
untested; see the README.
'docker': all OS-level resources are skipped (you run the Greenbone
Community Container compose stack yourself); only the GMP transport
credentials file is managed so the gvm_* providers still work.

Default value: `'unmanaged'`

##### <a name="-greenbone--manage_repo"></a>`manage_repo`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to manage the apt repository. Disable if you install Greenbone
packages through another mechanism (source build, distro packages, etc.).

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-greenbone--repo_location"></a>`repo_location`

Data type: `Pattern[/\Ahttps?:\/\/\S+\z/]`

Base URL of the apt repository to configure when manage_repo is true.

Default value: `'https://dl.greenbone.net/repo/CE/stable'`

##### <a name="-greenbone--repo_key_source"></a>`repo_key_source`

Data type: `Pattern[/\Ahttps?:\/\/\S+\z/]`

URL of the GPG signing key for the apt repository.

Default value: `'https://dl.greenbone.net/repo/CE/stable/greenbone-community-edition-keyring.gpg'`

##### <a name="-greenbone--repo_key_id"></a>`repo_key_id`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Expected GPG key fingerprint (long form, 40 hex chars). When set, apt
verifies the downloaded key matches this fingerprint before trusting it.
Strongly recommended to prevent a compromised origin from substituting
a rogue key. Obtain the current fingerprint from the Greenbone release page.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-greenbone--repo_release"></a>`repo_release`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Apt release component string (e.g. 'bookworm').

Default value: `$facts.dig('os', 'distro', 'codename')`

##### <a name="-greenbone--packages"></a>`packages`

Data type: `Hash[String, String]`

Hash of package name => ensure value to install.

Default value:

```puppet
{
    'gvmd'                => 'present',
    'gsad'                => 'present',
    'openvas-scanner'     => 'present',
    'ospd-openvas'        => 'present',
    'notus-scanner'       => 'present',
    'greenbone-feed-sync' => 'present',
    'pg-gvm'              => 'present',
  }
```

##### <a name="-greenbone--manage_packages"></a>`manage_packages`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to manage Greenbone OS packages. Disable when Greenbone is
installed from source or through an out-of-band packaging mechanism.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-greenbone--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\//]`

Path where the transport credentials YAML is written. It must be the path

(`Puppet[:confdir]` on the node). The default is the agent's own confdir,

### <a name="greenbone--admin"></a>`greenbone::admin`

Uses the gvm_admin custom type, which calls gvmd CLI via array-based
execution (no shell). The password is marked Sensitive and never appears as
plaintext in the compiled catalog, reports, or logs.

Note: gvmd requires --password as a CLI argument; the value therefore appears
in the process argv during the creation run. Rotate the bootstrap password
after initial provisioning.

Must run after gvmd is started and gvmd --migrate has completed.

### <a name="greenbone--database"></a>`greenbone::database`

Creates the gvm PostgreSQL user and gvmd database, installs the pg-gvm
extension, and runs `gvmd --migrate` once to initialise or upgrade the
schema. Requires the puppetlabs/postgresql module.

The `gvmd --migrate` exec runs as the gvm system user. PostgreSQL peer
authentication is used by default so no database password is required.

The dba superuser role is granted to the gvm database user only for the
duration of `gvmd --migrate` and revoked immediately afterward, so the
gvm process holds no persistent superuser membership at runtime.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `greenbone::database` class:

* [`db_name`](#-greenbone--database--db_name)
* [`db_user`](#-greenbone--database--db_user)
* [`gvm_user`](#-greenbone--database--gvm_user)

* [`gvmd_bin`](#-greenbone--database--gvmd_bin)
* [`migrate_timeout`](#-greenbone--database--migrate_timeout)
* [`psql_path`](#-greenbone--database--psql_path)
* [`migrate_script`](#-greenbone--database--migrate_script)
* [`migrate_sentinel`](#-greenbone--database--migrate_sentinel)

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\z/]`

Name of the PostgreSQL database. Must be a valid PostgreSQL identifier
(letters, digits, underscores; must start with a letter or underscore).

Default value: `'gvmd'`

System user used to run gvmd commands. Must be a valid POSIX username.

Default value: `$greenbone::gvm_user`

System group for gvmd. Must be a valid POSIX group name.

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\/[A-Za-z0-9_.\/\-]+\z/]`

### <a name="greenbone--feed"></a>`greenbone::feed`

Creates a systemd timer that runs greenbone-feed-sync on a configurable
schedule. Optionally triggers an immediate sync on the first Puppet run
via an Exec guarded by the presence of feed data.

The feed-sync service runs as $gvm_user under systemd sandboxing.
Write access is narrowed to $read_write_paths via ProtectSystem=strict.

The following parameters are available in the `greenbone::feed` class:

* [`sync_args`](#-greenbone--feed--sync_args)

* [`gvm_group`](#-greenbone--feed--gvm_group)

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\/[A-Za-z0-9_.\/\-]+\z/]`

Path to the greenbone-feed-sync binary. Must be an absolute path containing

Additional arguments passed to greenbone-feed-sync. Each element must

Run an immediate sync exec if no feed data is present yet.

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\/[A-Za-z0-9_.\/\-]+\z/]`

File whose existence indicates feed data has been synced at least once.

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\-]*\z/]`

System user the feed-sync service runs as. Must be a valid POSIX username.

##### <a name="-greenbone--feed--gvm_group"></a>`gvm_group`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\-]*\z/]`

System group for the feed-sync service. Must be a valid POSIX group name.

##### <a name="-greenbone--feed--read_write_paths"></a>`read_write_paths`

Data type: `Array[String]`

Paths granted write access under ProtectSystem=strict. Must cover all

### <a name="greenbone--ldap"></a>`greenbone::ldap`

Configures gvmd's `ldap_connect` authentication method over GMP. Greenbone
stores LDAP settings in its database (not a config file), so this class drives
the singleton `gvm_ldap` resource rather than writing a template.

Apply this only after the `greenbone` class (for the transport credentials) and
once gvmd is running, so the GMP `modify_auth` call succeeds. When included via
`greenbone::server` with `manage_ldap => true`, that ordering is wired for you.

Enabling LDAP lets nobody in by itself: each LDAP user must also exist in gvmd
as a gvm_user with `source => 'ldap_connect'`, and gets its role there.

#### Examples

##### Hiera data

```puppet
greenbone::ldap::ldaphost:   'ldap.example.org'
greenbone::ldap::authdn:     'uid=%s,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org'
greenbone::ldap::ldaps_only: true
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `greenbone::ldap` class:

* [`enable`](#-greenbone--ldap--enable)
* [`ldaphost`](#-greenbone--ldap--ldaphost)
* [`authdn`](#-greenbone--ldap--authdn)
* [`cacert`](#-greenbone--ldap--cacert)
* [`allow_plaintext`](#-greenbone--ldap--allow_plaintext)
* [`ldaps_only`](#-greenbone--ldap--ldaps_only)

##### <a name="-greenbone--ldap--enable"></a>`enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether LDAP authentication is enabled. false disables it without discarding
the stored host/DN.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-greenbone--ldap--ldaphost"></a>`ldaphost`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP server host name, optionally with :port -- not a URI; gvm-libs adds
ldap:// or ldaps:// itself. Required when enabling.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-greenbone--ldap--authdn"></a>`authdn`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Bind DN template with exactly one '%s', which gvmd replaces with the login
name, e.g. 'uid=%s,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org'. Required when enabling.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-greenbone--ldap--cacert"></a>`cacert`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

PEM CA certificate, used as the only trusted CA for the LDAP connection.
Leave unset to use the system trust store. A stored cacert cannot be
cleared over GMP; see gvm_ldap.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-greenbone--ldap--allow_plaintext"></a>`allow_plaintext`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to permit LDAP connections without TLS. Keep false unless you understand
the exposure.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-greenbone--ldap--ldaps_only"></a>`ldaps_only`

Data type: `Boolean`

Use ldaps (636) only instead of trying StartTLS on 389 first.

Default value: `false`

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-greenbone--redis--log_level"></a>`log_level`

Data type: `String`

Redis log level (debug, verbose, notice, warning). Named log_level rather
than loglevel because loglevel is a Puppet metaparameter.

Default value: `'notice'`

##### <a name="-greenbone--redis--maxmemory"></a>`maxmemory`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional Redis maxmemory limit (e.g. '512mb'). Unset by default.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-greenbone--redis--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\//]`

Path to the Redis configuration file managed by this class.

Default value: `'/etc/redis/redis-openvas.conf'`

##### <a name="-greenbone--redis--gvm_group"></a>`gvm_group`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\-]*\z/]`

System group for Greenbone services; granted access to the socket.

Default value: `$greenbone::gvm_group`

### <a name="greenbone--resources"></a>`greenbone::resources`

Include this class after the main `greenbone` class when you prefer
data-driven resource declarations over inline gvm_* resource blocks.

#### Examples

##### Hiera data

```puppet
greenbone::resources::schedules:
  weekly-monday-0200:
    icalendar: "BEGIN:VCALENDAR\nVERSION:2.0\n..."
    timezone: Europe/Berlin
greenbone::resources::targets:
  internal-network:
    hosts: '192.0.2.0/24'
    port_list_name: 'All IANA assigned TCP'
greenbone::resources::tasks:
  weekly-internal:
    target_name: internal-network
    config_name: 'Full and fast'
    schedule_name: weekly-monday-0200
greenbone::resources::scan_configs:
  'Full and fast (tuned)':
    base_config: 'Full and fast'
    scanner_preferences:
      expand_vhosts: '0'
greenbone::resources::filters:
  'Results (overrides applied)':
    term: 'apply_overrides=1 levels=chml rows=100 min_qod=70 first=1 sort-reverse=severity'
greenbone::resources::user_settings:
  'Results Filter':
    filter_name: 'Results (overrides applied)'
    setting_id: '739ab810-163d-11e3-9af6-406186ea4fc5'
greenbone::resources::groups:
  'Shared by admin':
    users: ['admin']
greenbone::resources::permissions:
  alice-super-on-admin:
    permission: 'Super'
    subject_type: 'user'
    subject_name: 'alice'
    resource_type: 'group'
    resource_name: 'Shared by admin'
greenbone::resources::overrides:
  tcp-timestamps-false-positive:
    nvt_oid: '1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.80091'
    new_severity: -1
    text: 'Assessed false positive: kernel randomises per-connection TCP timestamp offsets.'
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `greenbone::resources` class:

* [`schedules`](#-greenbone--resources--schedules)
* [`targets`](#-greenbone--resources--targets)
* [`tasks`](#-greenbone--resources--tasks)
* [`users`](#-greenbone--resources--users)
* [`user_settings`](#-greenbone--resources--user_settings)
* [`filters`](#-greenbone--resources--filters)
* [`groups`](#-greenbone--resources--groups)
* [`permissions`](#-greenbone--resources--permissions)
* [`scan_configs`](#-greenbone--resources--scan_configs)
* [`overrides`](#-greenbone--resources--overrides)

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--schedules"></a>`schedules`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_schedule resources, keyed by schedule name.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--targets"></a>`targets`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_target resources, keyed by target name.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--tasks"></a>`tasks`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_task resources, keyed by task name.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--users"></a>`users`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_user resources, keyed by username.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--user_settings"></a>`user_settings`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_user_setting resources, keyed as 'setting_name'. One naming a
filter from `filters` as its filter_name is ordered after it.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--filters"></a>`filters`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_filter resources, keyed by filter name.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--groups"></a>`groups`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_group resources, keyed by group name. Ordered after every
gvm_user, since members are referenced by name.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--permissions"></a>`permissions`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_permission resources, keyed by a Puppet-side name stored as a
marker in the permission comment (see the gvm_permission type docs).
Ordered after every gvm_user and gvm_group, which they name.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--scan_configs"></a>`scan_configs`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_scan_config resources, keyed by config name. A task naming one
of them as its config_name is ordered after it.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-greenbone--resources--overrides"></a>`overrides`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Hash of gvm_override resources, keyed by a Puppet-side name. A GVM override
has no name of its own, so that key is stored as a marker inside the
override text -- see the gvm_override type docs before choosing one, and
treat it as immutable once applied.

Default value: `{}`

### <a name="greenbone--server"></a>`greenbone::server`

Includes and `contain`s every Greenbone sub-class and wires the cross-class
ordering so the whole stack can be referenced as a single unit and applies
deterministically regardless of declaration order:

  greenbone -> database -> redis -> config -> service -> admin -> [ldap] -> feed

Configure each concern through its own class parameters (typically via Hiera).
The required credentials must be available for automatic class-parameter lookup
before including this class:
  * greenbone::password
  * greenbone::admin::password

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
include greenbone::server
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `greenbone::server` class:

* [`manage_ldap`](#-greenbone--server--manage_ldap)

##### <a name="-greenbone--server--manage_ldap"></a>`manage_ldap`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to include and order `greenbone::ldap` in the stack. Defaults to false;
set true and supply `greenbone::ldap::*` parameters (via Hiera) to manage the
LDAP authentication connection.

Default value: `false`

### <a name="greenbone--service"></a>`greenbone::service`

Controls ospd-openvas, notus-scanner, openvasd, gvmd, and gsad.
Start order matters: ospd-openvas and notus-scanner must be running
before gvmd starts, and gvmd must be running before gsad.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `greenbone::service` class:

* [`ensure`](#-greenbone--service--ensure)
* [`enable`](#-greenbone--service--enable)
* [`services`](#-greenbone--service--services)

##### <a name="-greenbone--service--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['running', 'stopped']`

Desired state for all services (running/stopped).

Default value: `'running'`

##### <a name="-greenbone--service--enable"></a>`enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to enable services at boot.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-greenbone--service--services"></a>`services`

Data type: `Hash[String, Hash]`

Override the set of managed services and their ordering constraints.
Keys are service names; value is a hash with optional 'require' list.

Default value:

```puppet
{
    'notus-scanner' => { require => [] },
    'ospd-openvas'  => { require => ['notus-scanner'] },
    'openvasd'      => { require => [] },
    'gvmd'          => { require => ['ospd-openvas', 'openvasd'] },
    'gsad'          => { require => ['gvmd'] },
  }
```

## Resource types

### <a name="gvm_admin"></a>`gvm_admin`

Ensures the initial GVM admin user exists via gvmd CLI. Uses array-based
execution (no shell) to prevent injection. The password is marked
sensitive and never stored as plaintext in the catalog. Note: gvmd CLI
passes --password in argv on creation; this is an unavoidable gvmd
limitation. Rotate the bootstrap password after provisioning.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_admin` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the user should exist. present creates it with `gvmd --create-user`; absent deletes it with `gvmd --delete-user`.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_admin` type.

* [`gvm_group`](#-gvm_admin--gvm_group)
* [`gvm_user`](#-gvm_admin--gvm_user)
* [`gvmd_bin`](#-gvm_admin--gvmd_bin)
* [`name`](#-gvm_admin--name)
* [`password`](#-gvm_admin--password)
* [`provider`](#-gvm_admin--provider)

##### <a name="-gvm_admin--gvm_group"></a>`gvm_group`

System group gvmd is run as.

Default value: `gvm`

##### <a name="-gvm_admin--gvm_user"></a>`gvm_user`

System user gvmd is run as, so it reaches its database with the right identity.

Default value: `gvm`

##### <a name="-gvm_admin--gvmd_bin"></a>`gvmd_bin`

Absolute path to the gvmd binary used to list, create and delete the user.

Default value: `/usr/sbin/gvmd`

##### <a name="-gvm_admin--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Name of the GVM user. Must not contain whitespace, <, >, &, or quotes.

##### <a name="-gvm_admin--password"></a>`password`

Admin password. Marked sensitive: not logged or stored as plaintext in catalog.

##### <a name="-gvm_admin--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `gvm_admin` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will usually
discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

### <a name="gvm_filter"></a>`gvm_filter`

Manages a saved GVM filter -- the named filter objects the web UI offers
in its filter dropdowns, and the thing a default-filter user setting points
at. Point a gvm_user_setting at one with `filter_name` to make it the
default for a page, e.g. 'Results Filter' for the report results view.

gvmd REWRITES THE TERM on create and modify, and this type canonicalizes
the manifest's term the same way so it does not churn. Measured against
gvmd 26.42 on 2026-10-20:

  * runs of whitespace collapse to one space;
  * a missing `first=`, `rows=` or `sort=`/`sort-reverse=` keyword is
    appended as `first=1`, `rows=10`, `sort=name`, in that order;
  * `rows=-1` is replaced by the user's Max Rows Per Page value.

The first two are reproduced here. The third depends on another setting,
so `rows=-1` is rejected instead -- write the row count you want.

Filters are matched by name. A filter made by hand in the web UI with the
same name is adopted; any other hand-made filter is never touched.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_filter` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Free-text comment shown in the web UI.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. Only `comment` can be cleared.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this filter should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `filter_type`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[a-z_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

GMP filter type, i.e. which kind of list it filters: result, report, task, target, override, ... Defaults to result.

Default value: `result`

##### `term`

Data type: `String`

The filter term, e.g. "apply_overrides=1 levels=chml rows=100 min_qod=70 first=1 sort-reverse=severity". Canonicalized as gvmd stores it; see the type docs.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_filter` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_filter--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_filter--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Filter name. gvmd rejects a second filter of the same name for the same owner.

### <a name="gvm_group"></a>`gvm_group`

Manages a GVM user group, matched by name. The group is owned by the
transport user.

The reason this type exists is Super permissions (see gvm_permission):
gvmd only lets a user grant Super on a resource it OWNS, and the
transport user owns neither its own user record nor any built-in role
(users.owner and roles.owner are NULL; measured on gvmd 26.42,
2026-10-20 -- "Super on user admin" is refused with "Permission
denied"). A group the transport user creates IS owned by it, and gvmd's
ACL honours "Super on a group the other user is a member of", so a group
holding the transport user is the resource to grant Super on.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_group` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Free-text comment shown in the web UI.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. Only `comment` can be cleared.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this group should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `users`

Data type: `Array[String]`

Member user names, compared as a set (order and duplicates ignored). gvmd stores them as one comma-separated list.

Default value: `[]`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_group` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_group--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_group--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Group name.

### <a name="gvm_ldap"></a>`gvm_ldap`

Manages the Greenbone LDAP (ldap_connect) authentication configuration via
GMP. gvmd keeps these settings in its database (the `meta` table), read and
written over GMP describe_auth / modify_auth. This is a singleton: declare
exactly one, titled "ldap_connect". ensure => present enables LDAP
authentication and pushes the connection settings; ensure => absent only
sets enable to false and keeps the stored host/DN.

What gvmd does with it (gvmd 26.42 / gvm-libs ldaputils.c): the login name
replaces `%s` in authdn. If the DN starts with `uid=`, gvmd first binds
anonymously and searches for the uid below the rest of the DN, falling back
to the template DN when the search finds nothing; then it does a simple
bind with the user's password. There is no bind account and no group
mapping -- each user must exist in gvmd with source ldap_connect (gvm_user),
and gets its role there.

LDAP is only one method: users with source file (the transport user, admin)
never touch LDAP and keep working when the directory is down.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_ldap` type.

##### `allow_plaintext`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether gvmd may fall back to an unencrypted connection when StartTLS fails. Leave false.

##### `authdn`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[^%]*%s[^%]*\z/]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

        Bind DN template with exactly one "%s", which gvmd replaces with the login
        name, e.g. "uid=%s,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org". gvmd rejects any other "%"
        at login time. Required when ensure => present.

##### `cacert`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

        PEM CA certificate gvmd uses as the ONLY trusted CA for the LDAP TLS
        connection. Unset means libldap's default trust store (the system CA
        bundle). Compared against what describe_auth returns. gvmd cannot clear a
        stored cacert over GMP (an empty value is rejected as an invalid
        certificate), so think before setting one: removing it from the
        manifest leaves it in place.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether LDAP authentication is enabled (present) or disabled (absent).

Default value: `present`

##### `ldaphost`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?\z/]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

LDAP server host name, optionally with :port -- NOT a URI; gvm-libs adds the scheme itself. Required when ensure => present.

##### `ldaps_only`

Data type: `Boolean`

Use ldaps (636) only. When false, gvmd tries StartTLS on 389 first and falls back to ldaps.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_ldap` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_ldap--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_ldap--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name of the auth method group. Use "ldap_connect".

### <a name="gvm_override"></a>`gvm_override`

Manages a GVM override: a rule that rewrites the severity GVM reports for a
given NVT, so a finding you have assessed and accepted stops colouring
every report. The common case is marking an assessed false positive, which
is `new_severity => -1`.

THE NAMEVAR IS A PUPPET-SIDE FICTION. A GVM override has no name -- GMP
identifies it by UUID alone, and `get_overrides` returns no name element
(verified against gvmd 26.37 on 2026-09-07). To make an override
addressable across runs, this type appends a marker line to the override's
text:

    <your text>

    [puppet:<resource title>]

and the provider recovers the title from it. Two consequences worth
knowing before using this type:

  * The marker is visible in the GVM web UI. That is deliberate -- an
    auditor reading an override sees which Puppet resource put it there.
  * An override WITHOUT the marker is invisible to this type. Overrides
    created by hand in the web UI are never read, updated or deleted by
    Puppet, and `puppet resource gvm_override` will not list them. Renaming
    the resource title orphans the old override rather than renaming it;
    set the old title to `ensure => absent` for one run to clean it up.

NOT SUPPORTED, deliberately: task- and result-scoped overrides, and
time-limited ones (GMP's `active` taking a day count). `active` here is a
boolean. All three are additive if they are ever needed; they were left out
because their GMP round-trip shape was not verified and an unverified
round-trip in a provider is what produces silent per-run churn.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_override` type.

##### `active`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the override is in effect. Maps to GMP active -1/0; time-limited overrides are not supported.

Default value: `true`

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this override should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `hosts`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated hosts/CIDRs this override is limited to. Undef applies it to every host. Whitespace around commas is normalized.

##### `new_severity`

Data type: `Numeric`

Severity to report instead. -1 is False Positive, 0 is Log; a positive value re-rates rather than clears. Defaults to -1 when not declared.

##### `nvt_oid`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

OID of the NVT this override applies to, e.g. 1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.80091. Pattern-constrained because it is interpolated into a GMP XML attribute.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Port this override is limited to, in GVM notation, e.g. "general/tcp". Undef applies it to every port.

##### `severity`

Data type: `Optional[Numeric]`

Only rewrite results whose current severity is this value. Undef applies the override at any severity.

##### `text`

Data type: `String`

Justification for the override. This is the audit trail -- say what was assessed and on what evidence. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped so a YAML block scalar does not churn.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_override` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_override--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_override--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Puppet-side identifier. Stored as a `[puppet:<name>]` marker in the override text; see the type docs.

### <a name="gvm_permission"></a>`gvm_permission`

Manages a GVM permission: the right named `permission` (a GMP command such
as get_tasks, or Super), granted to a user, role or group (the subject),
optionally limited to one named resource.

THE NAMEVAR IS A PUPPET-SIDE FICTION, as for gvm_override. A permission's
GMP `name` is the right it grants, not an identifier, so this type appends
a `[puppet:<title>]` marker to the permission comment and recovers the
title from it. Permissions without the marker -- the ~270 built-in ones
and any made in the web UI -- are never read, changed or deleted.

The common use is Super, which makes every object the resource's users own
visible and editable to the subject. gvmd only accepts Super on a resource
the creating user owns, and requires a resource (Super on everyone is
the Super Admin role, which GMP cannot assign). To share the transport
user's objects, grant Super on a gvm_group that contains the transport
user; see gvm_group for why the user itself does not work.

Subjects and resources are referenced by NAME and resolved to UUIDs on
write, so only named resource types work (user, role, group, task,
target, config, ...); a report has no name and cannot be addressed here.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_permission` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Why the permission exists. The marker is appended after it. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment']]]`

        Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an
        attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. Only `comment`
        can be cleared: the provider omits an unset resource, and whether
        modify_permission then drops the stored one is unverified, so to remove
        resource_type and resource_name, replace the permission.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this permission should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `permission`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The right granted: a GMP command name (get_tasks, modify_target, ...) or "Super". gvmd lower-cases command names and writes Super as "Super"; this type does the same so they compare.

##### `resource_name`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of that resource. Set together with resource_type.

##### `resource_type`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[a-z_]+\z/]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Type of the resource the permission is limited to. For Super it must be user, role or group. Undef grants the right on every resource of its kind (not allowed for Super).

##### `subject_name`

Data type: `String`

Name of the subject user, role or group.

##### `subject_type`

Data type: `Enum[user, role, group]`

Kind of subject the permission is granted to.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_permission` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_permission--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_permission--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Puppet-side identifier, stored as a [puppet:<name>] marker in the comment. Renaming orphans the old permission; ensure
=> absent it for one run first.

### <a name="gvm_scan_config"></a>`gvm_scan_config`

Manages a GVM scan config cloned from a feed config, and the scanner and NVT
preferences set on it.

WHY A CLONE: preferences can only be set on a config you own. The feed's
configs ("Full and fast" and friends) are not writable and modify_config
answers 400 on them. This type clones `base_config` once, under `name`, and
reconciles preferences onto the clone. A clone keeps the base's dynamic NVT
family selection, so it still picks up new checks as the feed grows.

PREFERENCES ARE A SUBSET, NOT THE WHOLE CONFIG. Only the preferences listed
in `scanner_preferences` and `nvt_preferences` are managed; every other
preference of the config (there are well over a thousand) is left as it is.
A listed preference changed in the web UI is set back on the next run.

GMP FACTS THIS TYPE IS BUILT ON (measured against gvmd 26.36):

  * Preference VALUES are base64-encoded on write. A bare value is accepted
    with a 200, stored as an empty string, and reads back as unset.
  * An NVT preference is WRITTEN under its qualified name
    "<oid>:<id>:<type>:<name>" -- the plain name is accepted with a 200 and
    silently stores the feed default -- but READ BACK under its plain name,
    with the OID as an attribute of <nvt>. That is why each
    `nvt_preferences` entry needs all five keys.
  * Because a 200 proves nothing here, every write is read back, and a
    value that does not read back as written fails the resource.

Renaming a config does not rename the clone: a new one is created under
the new name. Note that gvmd refuses to re-point a task that has already
run ("Status must be New to edit config").

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_scan_config` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this scan config should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `nvt_preferences`

Data type: `Array[Struct[{ oid => Pattern[/\A[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*\z/], id => String, type => String, name => String, value => String }]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

        NVT preferences to enforce. `id` and `type` come from the VT's own
        preference definition (get_nvts); all five keys are needed, see the type
        docs. The OID is pattern-constrained because it is interpolated into a GMP
        XML attribute.

Default value: `[]`

##### `scanner_preferences`

Data type: `Hash[String, String]`

Scanner preferences to enforce, by name, e.g. { "expand_vhosts" => "0" }. Values are strings, as GMP stores them.

Default value: `{}`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_scan_config` type.

* [`base_config`](#-gvm_scan_config--base_config)
* [`name`](#-gvm_scan_config--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_scan_config--base_config"></a>`base_config`

Data type: `String`

Name of the config to clone when this one does not exist yet, e.g. "Full and fast". Read only at creation; it must
exist, i.e. the feed must have synced.

Default value: `Full and fast`

##### <a name="-gvm_scan_config--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Name of the scan config. gvm_task refers to it by this name as config_name.

### <a name="gvm_schedule"></a>`gvm_schedule`

Manages a GVM scan schedule defined by an iCalendar string.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_schedule` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Human-readable description.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment']]]`

Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. Only `comment` can be cleared.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this schedule should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `icalendar`

Data type: `String`

Full iCalendar (RFC 5545) string defining the schedule. Must contain at least one VEVENT with a DTSTART and RRULE.

##### `timezone`

Data type: `String`

Timezone for the schedule (IANA tz database name).

Default value: `UTC`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_schedule` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_schedule--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_schedule--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Human-readable schedule name.

### <a name="gvm_target"></a>`gvm_target`

Manages a GVM scan target.

gvmd locks hosts, exclude_hosts, port_list_name and the three flags on a
target that any task references ("Target is in use"); only comment and
alive_test can change then. The provider sends only the attributes that
differ, so a locked attribute fails only when it really changes.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_target` type.

##### `alive_test`

Data type: `Optional[Enum["Scan Config Default","ICMP Ping","TCP-ACK Service Ping","TCP-SYN Service Ping","ARP Ping","ICMP & TCP-ACK Service Ping","ICMP & ARP Ping","TCP-ACK Service & ARP Ping","ICMP, TCP-ACK Service & ARP Ping","Consider Alive"]]`

Host alive detection method.

##### `allow_simultaneous_ips`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to scan all IPs of a host simultaneously.

Default value: `true`

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Human-readable description.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment', 'exclude_hosts']]]`

        Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an
        attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. `comment` and
        `exclude_hosts` can be cleared. gvmd refuses an exclude_hosts change on a
        target a task references, so clearing it fails then, like any other change
        to it. alive_test cannot be unset; set it to 'Scan Config Default' instead.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this scan target should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `exclude_hosts`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of hosts to exclude from the scan.

##### `hosts`

Data type: `String`

Comma-separated list of hosts, CIDRs, or ranges to scan.

##### `port_list_name`

Data type: `String`

Name of the GVM port list to use (e.g. "All IANA assigned TCP").

Default value: `All IANA assigned TCP`

##### `reverse_lookup_only`

Data type: `Boolean`

Scan only hosts that resolve to a hostname.

##### `reverse_lookup_unify`

Data type: `Boolean`

Deduplicate hosts that resolve to the same IP.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_target` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_target--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_target--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Unique name of the scan target.

### <a name="gvm_task"></a>`gvm_task`

Manages a GVM scan task.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_task` type.

##### `alterable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the task can be modified while running.

##### `auto_delete`

Data type: `Boolean`

When true, gvmd keeps only auto_delete_data most-recent reports and deletes older ones automatically. When false, all reports are kept.

##### `auto_delete_data`

Data type: `Integer[2, 1200]`

        Number of most-recent reports to keep when auto_delete is true (gvmd valid
        range: 2–1200). Ignored when auto_delete is false. Note: gvmd does not
        expose an API to reset this value to the "off" internal state (0) once set;
        to disable auto_delete on a task that previously had it enabled, delete and
        recreate the task.

Default value: `5`

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Human-readable description.

##### `config_name`

Data type: `String`

Name of the scan config to use (e.g. "Full and fast").

Default value: `Full and fast`

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment', 'schedule_name']]]`

        Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an
        attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. `comment` and
        `schedule_name` can be cleared; clearing schedule_name makes the task run on
        demand only. max_concurrency and max_hosts cannot be cleared: the provider
        omits an unset preference and gvmd keeps the stored value.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this scan task should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `hosts_ordering`

Data type: `Enum["sequential","random","reverse"]`

        Order in which target hosts are scanned. Note: gvmd silently ignores this
        value in modify_task and always returns "sequential" — "random"/"reverse"
        take effect at task creation only and cause perpetual Puppet drift
        thereafter. Leave at the default "sequential" unless creating a brand-new
        task and accepting the drift.

Default value: `sequential`

##### `max_concurrency`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

        Maximum number of concurrently executed NVTs per host (the openvas
        "max_checks" scanner preference; scanner default is 10). Lower this to
        reduce CPU load per host at the cost of a slower scan.

##### `max_hosts`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

        Maximum number of target hosts scanned simultaneously (the openvas
        "max_hosts" scanner preference; scanner default is 30). This is the dominant
        load lever: total peak concurrency is roughly max_hosts * max_concurrency.
        Lower it to keep the scanner from saturating the host.

##### `scanner_name`

Data type: `String`

Name of the scanner to use.

Default value: `OpenVAS Default`

##### `schedule_name`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of a GVM schedule. Unset means the task runs on demand only.

##### `target_name`

Data type: `String`

Name of the GVM scan target to scan.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_task` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_task--name)

##### <a name="-gvm_task--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Unique name of the scan task.

### <a name="gvm_user"></a>`gvm_user`

Manages a GVM user account.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_user` type.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['hosts']]]`

        Optional properties to clear on update, by attribute name. Removing an
        attribute from the manifest only stops Puppet managing it. Only `hosts` can
        be cleared, which gives the user access to all hosts.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this GVM user should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `hosts`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated list of hosts the user may access. Empty means all hosts.

##### `hosts_allow`

Data type: `Boolean`

When true, hosts list is an allowlist; when false it is a denylist.

Default value: `true`

##### `role_name`

Data type: `String`

Name of the GVM role to assign (e.g. "Admin", "User", "Observer").

Default value: `User`

##### `source`

Data type: `Enum[file, ldap_connect, radius_connect]`

        Authentication source for the user. "file" uses the local GVM password;
        "ldap_connect" / "radius_connect" delegate authentication to the configured
        LDAP / RADIUS server (see the greenbone::ldap class for the connection
        setup). For LDAP/RADIUS users the password is unused.

Default value: `file`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_user` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_user--name)
* [`password`](#-gvm_user--password)

##### <a name="-gvm_user--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

GVM username.

##### <a name="-gvm_user--password"></a>`password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

        User password. Write-only: sent on create and on every update, but because
        GMP never returns it the value cannot be compared, so changing only the
        password will NOT by itself trigger an update — combine a rotation with
        another attribute change, or recreate the user.

### <a name="gvm_user_setting"></a>`gvm_user_setting`

Manages a GVM user setting for the transport-authenticated user.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `gvm_user_setting` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this setting should exist. GMP settings cannot be deleted, so absent is rejected by the provider — always use present.

Default value: `present`

##### `filter_name`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

        Name of a saved filter (e.g. a gvm_filter) to point this setting at, for
        the web UI's default-filter settings such as 'Results Filter'. Resolved
        to the filter's UUID on write and compared by name on read, so the
        manifest never has to carry a UUID gvmd assigns. A gvm_filter of that
        name declared through greenbone::resources is ordered before it.

##### `value`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Setting value. Pass a UUID string for object-reference settings. Exactly one of value and filter_name must be set.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `gvm_user_setting` type.

* [`name`](#-gvm_user_setting--name)
* [`setting_id`](#-gvm_user_setting--setting_id)

##### <a name="-gvm_user_setting--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Setting name as returned by GMP get_settings.

##### <a name="-gvm_user_setting--setting_id"></a>`setting_id`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}\z/]]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

        UUID of the setting. Only needed for a setting gvmd does not list until it
        has been written once -- the web UI's default-filter settings are like
        that (verified 2026-10-20: 'Results Filter', 739ab810-163d-11e3-9af6-406186ea4fc5,
        was absent from get_settings, even when asked for by id, until set).
        Without it such a setting fails with "GVM setting not found".

## Functions

### <a name="greenbone--to_transport_yaml"></a>`greenbone::to_transport_yaml`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Serialise the three GMP transport credential fields to a YAML document using
Ruby's Psych library. This avoids handwritten quoting in an EPP template,
which cannot safely round-trip passwords that contain single/double quotes,
colons, newlines, or other YAML-significant characters.

The password may be passed as a Sensitive[String]; it is unwrapped inside the
function so the cleartext value never has to be unwrapped in the manifest
scope. The caller should wrap the returned YAML in Sensitive() when writing
it to a file so it does not leak into reports.

#### `greenbone::to_transport_yaml(String $user, Variant[String, Sensitive[String]] $password, String $socket)`

Serialise the three GMP transport credential fields to a YAML document using
Ruby's Psych library. This avoids handwritten quoting in an EPP template,
which cannot safely round-trip passwords that contain single/double quotes,
colons, newlines, or other YAML-significant characters.

The password may be passed as a Sensitive[String]; it is unwrapped inside the
function so the cleartext value never has to be unwrapped in the manifest
scope. The caller should wrap the returned YAML in Sensitive() when writing
it to a file so it does not leak into reports.

Returns: `String`

##### `user`

Data type: `String`



##### `password`

Data type: `Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]`



##### `socket`

Data type: `String`
